result.title: Divergence based Ranked Preference Alignment for LLMs
result.summary: Alignment of large language models typically relies on pairwise preference feedback, though ranked feedback can capture more comprehensive information across multiple responses within a single annotation. However, ranked-preference alignment is underexplored in practice compared to simpler pairwise approaches, potentially resulting in suboptimal behavior. Concurrently, recent research has conceptualized large language model alignment objectives as divergence estimators between aligned (preferred) and unaligned (less-preferred) response distributions, resulting in a family of objectives with an interpretable theoretical foundation and strong empirical performance. This work unifies these perspectives by introducing $f$-RPO, a $f$-divergence objective for ranked preference optimization that extends divergence-based alignment to ranked feedback and recovers pairwise preference alignment as a special case. Our theoretical analysis establishes rank-order consistency, showing that $f$-RPO preserves the underlying preference ordering at convergence. Empirical results indicate that total-variation and reverse-KL variants of the proposed objective consistently outperform ranked-alignment baselines in both ranking and generation quality across Qwen, Llama, & Gemma models ranging from 0.5B to 8B parameters.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 f-RPO，把 LLM 对齐目标统一为偏好与次优回复分布之间的 f-散度估计，并将这一框架从成对偏好扩展到多条回复的排序偏好反馈；理论部分证明其收敛时保持偏好次序，实验在 Qwen、Llama、Gemma（0.5B–8B）上比较各散度变体与排序对齐基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本对齐工作，与视觉状态生成无直接关系；但「单次标注内多条候选的排序偏好 + f-散度目标」可能为多条 latent 推理轨迹的排序监督与贡献分配提供可核查的目标设计线索。
